Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II scope for Hosted / Dedicated / Private

Hi Laura,

We're moving Redwood through our security review for the upcoming integration. Two quick asks to unblock procurement: 1) Can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers the three deployment modes we discussed (Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private/VPC or on-prem)? Specifically: which controls apply for each mode and whether the auditor's scope included any customer-managed infrastructure? 2) If full coverage isn't present for Dedicated/Private, would Redwood provide a bridge letter and can you describe the typical content/timing?

Hi Diana — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Rishi (security) and Vivek (legal) to provide precise language for you and Procurement. High-level answers below; Rishi will follow with the control-level mapping and suggested bridge letter text.

Quick summary (high-level):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Fully covered by our SOC 2 Type II scope for the audited period (2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30). Controls over our control plane, processes, and hosting layers are included.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Our SOC 2 covers the Redwood-managed control plane and inference runtime that we operate; however, Dedicated deployments may include customer-configurable networking or bring-your-own VPC elements. When the customer controls networking or customer-managed VMs exist, those layers fall outside Redwood's SOC 2 scope and are typically addressed via a bridge letter that clarifies responsibilities and any compensating controls.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: If Redwood is not managing the control plane or hardware (fully customer-hosted/on-prem), our SOC 2 does NOT attest to customer-managed environments. If Redwood provides a managed Private offering (we operate the control plane and certain services), we can scope those managed pieces into our attestation—this requires alignment with our auditors and confirmation of included services/audit period.

Rishi — can you provide the technical control mapping (network boundaries, data flow diagram) and a draft bridge letter template? Vivek — any legal caveats we should flag to Acme Procurement?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Hi Diana — thanks, and sorry for the quick follow-up. I pulled the control boundary diagram and a short FAQ into attachments; see the three items attached to this thread: redwood_soc2_type2_2024.pdf (excerpt, auditor's scope page), redwood_network_boundary.png (high-level prod network and control plane), and a draft bridge-letter-template.docx. Below are concrete clarifications you can pass to Procurement / Audit: 

1) Hosted API (our standard Hosted offering):
- What we cover: application hosting, runtime, deployment pipeline, key management integration points (where we manage keys), monitoring, incident response, and change management.
- Evidence available: SOC 2 Type II report for audit period 2024-07-01 to 2025-06-30; control testing summaries; auditor contact (bridgesecurity@auditco.com) for verification.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity / Redwood-managed):
- If Redwood provisions and operates the GPU pool, scheduler, model runtime, and the control plane (we manage node images and networking), those components were included in our SOC 2 testing.
- If the customer supplies VPCs, configures firewall rules, or maintains customer-owned hosts (BYO infra), those customer-owned controls were out of scope for our auditors. In those cases we provide a bridge letter that: (a) summarizes which controls remain in Redwood's responsibility, (b) lists controls the customer retains, and (c) suggests compensating controls the customer can evidence.

3) Private / VPC / On-prem (customer-hosted):
- When Redwood's software is installed in an air-gapped customer environment and Redwood has no operational access, SOC 2 does not cover that environment.
- For our managed Private offering (we run the control plane inside the customer's VPC or a managed on-prem appliance with remote attestation), we can discuss including those components in future SOC 2 cycles. That requires: (i) a scoping call with our auditors, (ii) at least 30–60 days lead time before the audit window to gather evidence, and (iii) contractual language confirming Redwood operational access for control testing.

Bridge letter specifics (typical contents):
- Statement of Redwood's audited period and what was included (control families, services, regions).
- Clear delineation of shared responsibility (what Redwood controls vs. customer controls).
- If controls have changed since the audit period, a short note describing the change and compensating controls or a timeline for the next attestation.
- Contact info for our auditor for independent verification.

Timing: We can issue a standard bridge letter within 5–7 business days after legal review (signature + auditor notification). If Acme requires auditor-signed confirmation or extended wording, that can add time depending on AuditCo availability.

Next steps I propose:
- Acme to confirm which deployment(s) you'll use in production (Hosted, Dedicated managed by Redwood, or Private).
- If Dedicated/Private: provide a brief network/ops diagram and identify any customer-managed components so we can finalize bridge language.
